input.claim_text: On 3 September 2023 I woke up to find my front fence and letterbox spray painted with some kind of symbol, and one of the timber palings had been kicked in. I'm not sure exactly when it happened overnight, and I didn't hear anything, but it definitely wasn't like that when I went to bed. My policy number is HM-773245 and I'd guess it'll cost around $850 to repaint and replace the paling.

output.cause: unknown vandalism on front fence and letterbox

input.query: Is vandalism or malicious damage to fences covered?

output.answer:
Based on the excerpts provided, vandalism or malicious damage is covered under Insured Event 8 ("Malicious Damage, Intentional Damage or damage by vandals"), which states the policy will "Cover for loss or damage to the Insured Property...as a result of Malicious Damage, Intentional Damage or damage by vandals" [RAA Contents PDS, page 47]. Fences are not specifically excluded from this Insured Event — the listed exclusions for Malicious Damage cover only: chips, scratches, dents or superficial markings; wear and tear or damage over time; damage caused by you, your Guest, an Occupier or a Co-Insured; damage caused by a person who entered with consent of you, your Guest, an Occupier or a Co-Insured; or loss/damage not reported to the police [RAA Contents PDS, page 47].

Note that a separate exclusion exists elsewhere in the policy for wind damage to gates or fences that are not structurally sound or properly maintained [RAA Contents PDS, page 45], but this exclusion appears in the context of a different Insured Event (not the Malicious Damage section) and is not stated to apply to vandalism/malicious damage claims.

The excerpts do not contain a complete list of General Exclusions that might also apply across all Insured Events, so I cannot confirm with certainty that no other policy-wide exclusion affects fence cover for malicious damage. Based solely on what is provided, malicious damage/vandalism to fences would be covered under Insured Event 8, subject to the specific exclusions listed at [RAA Contents PDS, page 47].

However, the same policy section explicitly excludes cover for "loss/damage not reported to the police" [RAA Contents PDS, page 47]. The claim narrative gives no indication of whether the policyholder reported the vandalism to police, and this is a key fact that determines whether coverage applies. Because the required information isn't available and the outcome hinges on it, I cannot confirm coverage without guessing, so this needs human review to confirm whether a police report was filed (and to resolve the fence/contents-vs-building classification, since the retrieved cover was sourced from the Contents PDS despite the fence typically being a building item) before payout can be calculated with the excess/coverage limit already on file ($500 excess / $45,000 limit).
